source: Fresh independent Codex review of the prefix-state correction.
problem: The Python matcher identifies any bare |-damage| line after an earlier switch/boost as a direct defender hit. A self HP cost such as Substitute is bare damage but is not a damage roll against the acting move's opponent, so the mapper intentionally emits no legal_roll_state and strict matching incorrectly skips the branch.
required_mechanism: Track the acting side from the most recent |move| line.
Treat a bare |-damage| line as a repricing target only when its target side differs from that acting side.
Keep same-side bare HP costs on the ordinary pre-state path; do not synthesize a snapshot and do not change component attribution.
regression_prediction: Calm Mind followed by the opponent's Substitute must not load a branch-local state or raise BranchLegalRollError merely because the Substitute HP cost follows the boost.
containment: Do not change the Rust prefix snapshot mechanism.
Do not widen accepted damage supports, attribution, residual handling, or divergence classes.
Continue to fail closed whenever an actual opponent-hit branch requires but lacks legal_roll_state.
